subject.title: Windows: lstat bottleneck causes 2-3x slower performance vs Mac (59% of CPU time)

question: Should OpenClaw accept operation-scoped realpath and existing-ancestor caches inside plugin hook, plugin skill, and sandbox containment checks for this Windows lstat performance fix?
rationale: The remaining implementation path changes cache lifetime around security-sensitive path containment, which is a maintainer security tradeoff rather than a mechanical bug repair decision.

options.title: Accept operation-scoped caches
options.body: Land the linked candidate or a maintainer replacement once exact-head checks stay green and the cache scope is explicitly accepted.

options.title: Limit optimization to non-containment paths
options.body: Reject cache reuse in plugin/sandbox containment checks and keep only metadata or other non-boundary performance work.

options.title: Require refreshed Windows profile first
options.body: Ask for latest-head Windows startup profiling before making the cache-lifetime decision.

recommendation.title: Accept operation-scoped caches
recommendation.body: Land the linked candidate or a maintainer replacement once exact-head checks stay green and the cache scope is explicitly accepted.
